Forecast Discussion

Cold high pressure moves across the Great Lakes today. Skies are clear, and temperatures peak early this afternoon and then fall slowly. Tonight is dry and cold.

Wednesday, the high moves into New England and wedges cold air down the east side of the Appalachians. Clouds thicken quickly. Light rain is possible as early as the morning and spreads from the south in the afternoon. The highest elevations may see a brief mix with snow or ice as it begins.

Low pressure moves along the Gulf Coast Wednesday and up the East Coast on Thanksgiving Day. An easterly wind between the high and the low pushes moisture up the Blue Ridge. Rain is heavy at times Wednesday night, heaviest near the Blue Ridge. It may still be heavy early Thursday morning, then tapers off in the afternoon.

An upper-level low is in northeast Arkansas early Thursday morning, but instead of digging into the Southeast, it moves northeast into the Ohio Valley (and eventually eastern Canada). That northeast track and unfavorable temperatures aloft limit the wrap-around snow showers we can get out of the system.

Much colder air follows Thursday night on gusty winds. A few evening showers give way to flurries or snow showers after midnight, mostly on the west side of the Appalachians and at higher elevations.

Friday is cold and windy with flurries, again mostly west and at higher elevations. Snow showers or flurries linger Friday evening. Accumulations are very limited, an inch or so at higher western elevations.

High pressure builds over the Southeast Saturday. It is dry, windy early, and not as cold by afternoon.

Sunday is milder with increasing clouds as a cold front approaches, and a shower is possible late in the day. Rain falls Sunday night, and showers end Monday morning.
